title: Coupling Single Electrons to Single Photons and Probing their Entanglement
content: Electron beams are a formidable tool for probing nanophotonic systems [1]. Combining electron microscopy with external optical excitation in ultrafast transmission electron microscopes has enabled the mapping of optical near-fields [2] and the bunching of electrons in attosecond pulses [3, 4]. These developments are based on the stimulated inelastic scattering between electrons and light [5, 6], in which the electrons gain energy from or lose energy to the optical field. Recently, the underlying interaction strength of this process has been increased significantly by harnessing resonant enhancement of the optical field and velocity phase matching [7]. Such an increased interaction strength also benefits the spontaneous scattering of electrons with light, thus promising applications like generating complex quantum states of light [8].
